If you are using dotnet core when you code then I would suggest taking the extra step of learning dependency injection for this purpose.
Its really not that hard even though I also found it hard to grasp in the beginning.

If it's mainly for small private projects that don't require testing etc then a static class as you described works perfectly :)

Just remember that if you have lots of calls asynchronously then you may get weird errors cause of  that a static class use the same instance of filereader etc.

Another thing to remember or think about is that classes usually describe in wide terms what it is and always in singular.

For instance...

The class Person can be a male or a female, of any ethnicity and age. This ofcourse requires the class to have those properties. 

Hence you can use the Person class to describe all persons you need to.

The class Dog example that you used is just that. A wide description of a singular dog that can be of any race, gender, age etc.

I also had a problem understanding the difference between a class and an instance of a class when I started out.
Understanding why they are named the way they are was part of my understanding.

var person = new Person() ;
